entries.title: View Items for Historical Measures
body: You can view historical measure conditions for items in a dashboard widget. The items that match the condition are displayed in the state they were in during the specified time period.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Items in a Widget Segment.

entries.title: Filter Evaluation Time in Historical Data
body: The Filter Evaluation Time setting is available when viewing historical data in dashboard widgets and reports. The following settings are available:

- Current State: Filters evaluate data based on the most recent state. Historical data is displayed for entities that currently meet the filter criteria, regardless of their state during the selected date range.

- Historical State: Filters are applied for a selected date range, or for each time bucket if a date breakdown is selected. Only records that met the filter criteria at those relevant points in time are displayed.
To learn more, see Understanding Historical Data.
The Filter Evaluation Time setting is available in the following locations:
- When configuring historical custom dashboards.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Configuring Custom Dashboards.
- When configuring historical reports.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Creating Reports.

entries.title: Qualys Global AssetView Connector Available
body: The Qualys Global AssetView (GAV) connector gives you a broad view of discovered and inventoried assets in your environment, regardless of whether they have been scanned for vulnerabilities. It uses sensors, such as cloud agents or passive sensors, to continuously track all assets.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Qualys GAV Connector.

entries.title: GitHub Repositories App Token Authentication
body: You can authenticate the GitHub Repositories connector using a GitHub App installation token. This method allows for centrally managed, organization-level access that can be scoped to specific repositories and least-privileged permissions. This method is not tied to an individual user account, and uses short-lived tokens to reduce exposure and simplify revocation.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the GitHub Repositories Connector.

entries.title: Exploding JSON Structures in Data Source Mapping
body: Data source mapping supports exploding JSON structures to create one output record per array element. You can use one of the following methods:
- Expand a parent JSON object to reveal its nested fields, then explode an internal array to create a single record per element in the array.
- See image.
- Explode an array of objects to create a single record per object. You can then either map the entire object, or expand it to reveal and map the unique nested keys found across the array elements.
- See image.
When a field is exploded, you must incorporate the exploded value into a composite key mapping to preserve record uniqueness and prevent overwrites. Only one field can be exploded per mapping.
To learn more, see Mapping Data Sources.

entries.title: Overview Dashboard
body: The Overview dashboard provides a comprehensive view of findings from ingestion to remediation. It demonstrates deduplication, normalization, and prioritization capabilities that transform fragmented data points into a streamlined set of prioritized work items based on your defined business context.
The Overview dashboard includes the following elements:

- The primary view of the dashboard demonstrates the transition of high-volume findings from their raw source state to their final, prioritized, grouped state in tickets. The flow concludes with a breakdown of tickets by risk-adjusted severity, featuring integrated Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) metrics for each category.

- The tiles at the bottom of the dashboard track key metrics including total vulnerable assets, unique CVE counts, ticket assignment percentages, and the status of third-party system integrations to monitor program health and identify workflow bottlenecks.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Overview Dashboard.

entries.title: Ticket Workflows Enhancements
body: Zscaler Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM) Ticket Workflows allow more granular control of ticket statuses by simplifying rule creation and improving automation logic. Enhancements include:

- Enable and disable individual rules: Each workflow rule can be saved in an active or inactive state. This allows you to prepare rules in advance and activate them only when ready, or to temporarily disable a rule's logic without deleting its configuration.
- See image.

- Set a default status for all new tickets: You can define a default status that is automatically assigned to newly created tickets that don't meet the criteria for another rule. This ensures that no ticket is created without a status, which helps improve process compliance.
- See image.

- Automatic ticket closure rule: Instead of targeting all tickets that are not closed, you can specify which statuses to exclude from the rule. This makes it easier to target only active tickets for auto-closure.
- See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Ticket Workflows.

entries.title: Dashboard and Report Tags
body: You can create and assign tags to dashboards and reports in the Agentic Security Operations Platform. You can use these tags to filter and locate dashboards and reports.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Custom Dashboards and Creating Reports.

entries.title: Mapping Copilot for Data Sources
body: Mapping Copilot is an AI-guided mapping assistant available in the Agentic Security Operations Platform (SecOps Platform). It provides context-aware mapping recommendations to align third-party source data to the SecOps data model based on source-run characteristics (e.g., field names, data types, and value patterns), integration metadata, existing mapping connections, and platform guidelines. Mapping Copilot helps reduce manual mapping, identify the target SecOps entity type, map the key identifier fields, and proposes complex transformation scripts.
You can interact with Mapping Copilot through a chat interface on the mapping page of a data source. Mappings generated through the assistant are marked with an AI icon.
Availability of Mapping Copilot is controlled by the account admin. Mapping Copilot requires at least one successful source run within the last 90 days.
See image.
To learn more, see Using Mapping Copilot and Mapping Data Sources.

entries.title: Google Cloud Storage Outegration
body: The Google Cloud Storage outegration is used as a report delivery method to dispatch files from the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform applications (e.g., UVM) to your Cloud Storage bucket.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Google Cloud Storage Outegration.

entries.title: Integrated External Attack Surface Management Capabilities
body: Zscaler integrates External Attack Surface Management (EASM) capabilities into the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform to provide native asset inventory and vulnerability management for internet-facing assets. This integration offers automated discovery and scanning of internet-exposed assets, starting from admin-configured seeds (i.e., known, verified assets), to map an organization's digital infrastructure, analyze internet exposure, and detect associated vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. The scanned asset and finding information is automatically merged with the context-rich data and native capabilities supported by the SecOps platform to provide comprehensive visibility and enriched security insights, helping organizations secure their assets and remediate risks from a centralized platform.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Zscaler EASM Capabilities, Understanding Asset Discovery with Zscaler EASM, and Configuring Discovery Settings.

entries.title: Preserved Ticket Scope for Exception Requests
body: Tickets with exception requests are locked for manual split and merge actions to preserve the scope of the exception under review. If all exceptions for a ticket are closed or in a Closed status bucket, manual split and merge actions become available again. Admins or users with Exceptions - Audit permission can still split and merge findings and tickets.
See image.
To learn more, see Requesting Exceptions.

entries.title: Apache Kafka Outegration
body: The Apache Kafka outegration enables Zscaler Data Fabric for Security to publish entity data to an external Kafka topic. This provides a secure, reliable way for you to ingest ticket events into event-driven architectures.
To learn more, see Configuring the Apache Kafka Outegration.

entries.title: Trigger Asset Scans
body: You can trigger asset scans directly in UVM to immediately validate remediation, instead of waiting for scheduled scan cycles. With a configured scanner outegration, you can launch scans from the Assets page, an asset drawer, or a ticket drawer while reviewing remediation tasks. These scans check whether the asset's reported findings are remediated or still active, and scan results are automatically synchronized back into UVM.
See image.

Supported scanners include Tenable Vulnerability Management (formerly Tenable.io) and Tenable Security Center (on‑premises). The Tenable scanner outegration offers default mapping to send asset IP addresses directly to Tenable. To learn more, see Configuring the Tenable Outegration.
To learn more, see Triggering Asset Scans in UVM.

entries.title: Remediation Copilot for UVM
body: Remediation Copilot is an AI-guided remediation assistant available directly in UVM tickets. It provides context-aware fix paths and instructions based on the ticket's findings, affected assets, and environment, and suggests mitigations when no fix is available. Remediation Copilot helps close the gap between detection and resolution, including cases where external sources do not provide clear guidance.
Users can interact with Remediation Copilot via an in-ticket chat and save a summary of steps to the ticket's Fixes tab for traceability, handoffs, and audits.

Availability of Remediation Copilot is controlled by the account admin. Data shared with the assistant stays within Zscaler services, and personally identifiable information (PII) is stripped where possible.
See image.
To learn more, see What Is Remediation Copilot? and Using Remediation Copilot.

entries.title: Calculate Ticket SLA Based on Active Findings
body: You can calculate the service level agreement (SLA) for a ticket based only on its active findings. Ticket SLA is calculated based on the earliest SLA date of its findings, so this option helps teams focus remediation timelines on findings that still require action, and avoid SLA dates being driven by inactive findings. If all findings in a ticket are inactive, the ticket SLA remains populated with its most recent value.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Service Level Agreement Settings.

entries.title: Microsoft Entra ID Stream Data Update
body: The Entra ID - Devices stream retrieves registered owners for each device, in addition to the device inventory data (e.g., device ID, name, operating system, and compliance and management fields).
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

entries.title: Wiz Assets Connector Available
body: The Wiz Assets stream retrieves detailed information about cloud resources from the Wiz platform. It can optionally enrich this data with network exposure information.
To learn more, see Configuring the Wiz Connector.

entries.title: Microsoft Entra ID Applications Stream Available
body: The Microsoft Entra ID connector includes the Applications stream that retrieves a list of applications registered in your Microsoft Entra ID tenant (e.g., application name and app ID) and the owners for each application.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

entries.title: Dragos Connector Available
body: The Dragos connector enables organizations to retrieve Operational Technology (OT) asset inventories and their associated vulnerabilities from the Dragos platform via the Sitestore API. It provides detailed metadata, including asset details, vulnerability severities, timestamps, and CVE identifiers to help teams identify affected systems and assess operational criticality.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Dragos Connector.

entries.title: HCL BigFix Computers Connector Available
body: The HCL BigFix - Computers connector retrieves a list of computers from your HCL BigFix deployment, including key details such as computer IDs, hostnames, operating systems, IP addresses, and core properties like hardware information.
To learn more, see Configuring the HCL BigFix Computers Connector.

entries.title: SentinelOne Connector Streams Available
body: The SentinelOne connector has three new streams available:
- SentinelOne Assets: Retrieves different types of assets based on configuration, including endpoints such as managed devices, cloud assets, and unmanaged devices discovered on the network.

- SentinelOne Alerts: Retrieves security alerts from the SentinelOne Singularity platform, allowing for centralized security monitoring, threat analysis, and incident response in the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform.
- SentinelOne CNS Findings: Retrieves vulnerabilities and cloud/IT misconfigurations configured in the SentinelOne Singularity platform's Extended Security Posture Management (xSPM) module.
To learn more, see Configuring the SentinelOne Connector.

entries.title: Mandiant ASM Connector Available
body: The Mandiant ASM connector allows organizations to retrieve data from Mandiant's Attack Surface Management platform across two streams:

- Mandiant ASM Entities: Retrieves all exposed assets within the organization's external attack surface, including domains, subdomains, IP addresses, hostnames, URLs, and associated Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS) certificates.

- Mandiant ASM Issues: Retrieves detailed issues, such as misconfigurations, open ports, vulnerabilities with severity levels, and SSL/TLS-related weaknesses, along with their statuses and remediation recommendations.
To learn more, see Configuring the Mandiant ASM Connector.

entries.title: Ticket Workflows Enhancements
body: Ticket Workflows in Zscaler Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM) have been redesigned to organize rules into three workflow categories:
- Ticket Status Management: Centralizes automated rules for closing tickets, creates or reopens tickets for resurfaced findings, and defines custom status transitions.

- Lock Ticket Scope Triggers: Defines conditions (e.g., manual ticket splits or merges) that automatically lock a ticket's scope to prevent subsequent automated system logic from modifying its findings, ensuring ticket integrity.
- Auto-Dispatch to External Systems: Triggers third-party work items and alerts based on specific ticket criteria.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Ticket Workflows.

entries.title: Exploding Array Fields in Data Source Mapping
body: Data source mapping supports exploding a single source array field into multiple mapped output records, with one output record created per array element. Only one field can be exploded per mapping. When a field is exploded, the exploded value must be included in the entity key to preserve record uniqueness and prevent overwrites during data unification. This can be done by incorporating the exploded field into a composite key mapping.
See image.
To learn more, see Mapping Data Sources.

entries.title: Updated Severity and Service Level Agreement Settings in UVM
body: Zscaler Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM) features enhanced severity settings and service level agreement (SLA) settings for improved flexibility and control.
See image.

Severity settings are independent of SLA settings, allowing you to map severity score ranges to severity categories with a built-in validation mechanism to ensure complete coverage and accurate classification.
See image.

The updated SLA settings enable you to define resolution timelines for findings or tickets with more control and precision. You can set global countdown triggers in the configuration and override them in individual rules for specific scenarios. Custom SLA rules allow you to define timelines based on conditions like severity, asset type, or business unit, while default SLA rules provide fallback timelines when no custom rules apply. Dynamic SLA updates ensure deadlines stay accurate by recalculating automatically when attributes like severity or ownership change.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Severity Categories and Configuring Service Level Agreement Settings.

entries.title: Aqua Security Connector Available
body: The Aqua Security connector enables organizations to retrieve comprehensive data from Aqua Security's cloud-native security platform across 7 data streams. These streams include insights into vulnerability data for functions, hosts, and container images, as well as details about running containers and cloud misconfigurations, compliance violations, and security alerts. They also retrieve metadata about managed hosts and container images, offering detailed information for effective security management.
To learn more, see Configuring the Aqua Security Connector.

entries.title: Saved Views in Widgets View Items
body: You can save customized table layouts when viewing widget items, including reordering, adding, or removing columns. Saved views are automatically reusable across all widgets and dashboards that reference the same entity (e.g., Tickets, Assets, or custom entities), increasing consistency and efficiency in data exploration.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Items in a Widget Segment.

entries.title: Automated Aging of Findings for Inactive Assets
body: When configuring asset aging, you can choose to automatically age findings linked to inactive assets. This ensures alignment between the status of assets and their associated findings, minimizes discrepancies, reduces manual cleanup, and improves data consistency. This process applies alongside the aging logic of findings configured in a source's remediation detection settings, with either configuration being sufficient to age the findings.
See image.
To learn more, see Aging Assets and Creating Data Sources.

entries.title: Rapid7 InsightVM Policy Compliance Stream Available
body: The Rapid7 Policy Compliance stream ingests policy compliance data from the Rapid7 InsightVM platform. The data is retrieved via asynchronous export jobs and downloaded as Parquet files.
To learn more, see Configuring the Rapid7 InsightVM Connector.

entries.title: Veracode Applications Stream Available
body: The Veracode connector has one new stream available. The Veracode Applications stream retrieves a paginated list of applications from Veracode.
To learn more, see Configuring the Veracode Connector.

entries.title: Testing Component for Mapping Scripts
body: The Script Editor in the Security Operations Platform (SecOps Platform) includes a testing component that runs your Python mapping logic against representative ingested source records, and previews the value returned for the target SecOps Platform field. This helps you validate transformations, fallback logic, and edge cases before finalizing a mapping. The Test Logic panel uses sample records from the most recent successful ingestion run (the full dataset if the last successful run is within 90 days; otherwise, a 50-record preview), and dynamically generates inputs based on the source fields referenced in your script. You can also populate inputs from a sample record or manually enter values. Scripts evaluate a source row provided as a dictionary (row), supporting access patterns such as row["field"] and row.get("field").
See image.
To learn more, see Mapping Data Sources.

entries.title: Endor Labs Connector Available
body: The Endor Labs connector allows organizations to retrieve findings from specified namespaces in the Endor Labs platform, including vulnerabilities using the REST API, as well as Software Composition Analysis (SCA) findings, container-related findings, secrets-related findings, and Static Application Security Testing (SAST) findings using the Query API. The connector retrieves detailed metadata like severity, timestamps, and remediation actions, with the Query API streams supporting data retrieval from a namespace and its child namespaces.
To learn more, see Configuring the Endor Labs Connector.

entries.title: Ticket Lifecycle
body: Ticket Lifecycle allows you to define the behavior of tickets throughout their lifecycle. This enables clarity, control, and automation for every stage of ticket progression. Ticket Lifecycle contains the following settings:
- Ticket Statuses: Manage the status of tickets by creating status buckets.
- Ticket Workflows: Configure automated rules to manage progression of ticket statuses and dispatch of tickets to external systems.
To learn more, see Managing Ticket Statuses in UVM and Configuring Ticket Workflows.

entries.title: Enable Failure Alert Notifications for ETL, Connectors, and Outegrations
body: You can enable email notifications to receive alerts on errors for outegration workflows, source run failures, and issues with Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) and data pipeline. This allows you to proactively resolve issues and reduce workflow disruptions.
To learn more, see Enabling Email Notifications for Failures.

entries.title: GitHub Advanced Security Connector Available
body: There are two available GitHub Advanced Security streams:
- GitHub Advanced Security - Code Scanning: Retrieves code scanning data from GitHub repositories, including security vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and potential exploits in codebases.

- GitHub Advanced Security - Secret Scanning: Retrieves secret scanning data from GitHub repositories, including exposed sensitive information such as API keys, credentials, and tokens in both public and private repositories.
To learn more, see Configuring the GitHub Advanced Security Connector.

entries.title: Ionix Connector Available
body: The Ionix connector enables organizations to retrieve critical data from two streams: Assets and Findings. The connector supports retrieving detailed metadata, including asset IDs, types, statuses, and vulnerabilities. For the Findings stream, the connector retrieves CVE-level details and associated remediation actions, and supports incremental data synchronization.
To learn more, see Configuring the Ionix Connector.

entries.title: Dimension-Based Formatting Rules
body: Dimension-based formatting rules allow you to define custom coloring for a dimension and apply the rules to specific widgets. This helps make dashboard data more intuitive and easier to grasp at a glance.
See image.
To learn more, see Creating Formatting Rules.

entries.title: Audit Logs
body: Audit logs track user-initiated actions within the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform. This enables you to monitor configuration changes, such as updates to reports, data source instances, and outegrations. You can download specific audit logs for immediate review, and schedule automated hourly or daily exports to an external destination such as an Amazon S3 bucket.
To learn more, see Viewing Audit Logs.

entries.title: GitHub Repositories Connector Available
body: The GitHub Repositories connector enables organizations to ingest data from GitHub for the specified repositories. It retrieves repository metadata and includes configuration options such as selecting the repository branch to use and ingesting repository custom properties defined in your GitHub organization.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the GitHub Repositories Connector.

entries.title: Claroty xDome Healthcare Connector Available
body: The Claroty xDome for Healthcare (formerly Medigate) connector allows organizations to retrieve security posture data for medical devices, OT, and IoT assets across two streams:

- Claroty xDome Healthcare - Assets: Retrieves device information, including network and device details, vulnerabilities, and risk scores, as well as visibility and security posture data such as last seen and scan times, end-of-life status, and authentication user lists.

- Claroty xDome Healthcare - Vulnerabilities: Retrieves vulnerability data including severity scores, affected products and devices, exploitability data, and recommendations for remediation, as well as vulnerability status and assignment details.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Claroty xDome for Healthcare Connector.
